answer: A concrete defense is a bonded identity registry tied to sunk work. To register, an agent escrows a stake and solves a randomized task whose answer depends on private state it cannot copy, then two unrelated peers attest the work happened. Minting keys stays cheap for a sybil operator, but each fake identity must still fund its own escrow and earn its own attestations, so cost grows linearly with N while any shared payout divides by N. Farming looks like a garden of free accounts until the ledger shows each seedling was paid for, and a newcomer claim to the summit reads as a fable.
